desc: Parse the input to extract $N$, $M$, and the list of pre-colored cells, storing them in separate lists for 'B' and 'W' constraints.

Initialize arrays/lists to track the minimum required prefix length ($min\_row[i]$, $min\_col[j]$) and maximum allowed prefix length ($max\_row[i]$, $max\_col[j]$) for each row and column, initialized to 0 and $N$ respectively.
Iterate through the 'B' constraints: for a black cell at $(x, y)$, update $min\_row[x-1] = \max(min\_row[x-1], y)$ and $min\_col[y-1] = \max(min\_col[y-1], x)$.
Iterate through the 'W' constraints: for a white cell at $(x, y)$, update $max\_row[x-1] = \min(max\_row[x-1], y-1)$ and $max\_col[y-1] = \min(max\_col[y-1], x-1)$.
Validate individual row and column constraints: check if $min\_row[i] > max\_row[i]$ or $min\_col[j] > max\_col[j]$ for any $i, j$. If so, output "No".

Refine $max\_row[i]$ using column upper bounds: for each column $j$ with $max\_col[j] < N$, update $max\_row[i] = \min(max\_row[i], j-1)$ for all $i > max\_col[j]$. Since $N$ is large, this must be done efficiently (e.g., by checking only relevant $i$ or using the property that $max\_row[i]$ is non-increasing).

Identify critical points for coordinate compression: collect all $L_i, R'_i+1, A_j, B_j+1$ (where $L_i=min\_row[i], R'_i=max\_row[i], A_j=min\_col[j], B_j=max\_col[j]$). Add $1$ and $N+1$. Sort and deduplicate.

Compute $cap(j)$ for each interval: $cap(j)$ is the count of rows $i$ such that $L_i \le j \le R'_i$. This can be computed by sorting the intervals $[L_i, R'_i]$ and using a sweep-line or prefix sums on the compressed coordinates.

Perform the greedy check from $j=N$ down to $1$ over the compressed intervals. Maintain $f(j+1)$, compute $f(j)$ using the recurrence $f(j) = \min(B, f(j+1) + cap \times \text{length})$, and verify $f(j) \ge A$ and $B \ge f(j+1)$.
If all checks pass, output "Yes"; otherwise, output "No".
